topStories.headline: Valencia Street Cannabis Café Would Be Bay Area's First, as SF's New Law Takes Hold
topStories.dek: A Mission District operator is now on track to open an Amsterdam-style cannabis café on Valencia Street after Mayor Lurie signed landmark legislation last month.
topStories.body:
The Mission District may soon be home to the Bay Area's first Amsterdam-style cannabis café, after Mayor Daniel Lurie signed an ordinance implementing Assembly Bill 1775, a 2024 state law that allows cannabis shops to serve food, nonalcoholic beverages, and host live entertainment. The ordinance was introduced in March by District 8 Supervisor and Board President Rafael Mandelman.

William Dolan, who has sought to open a cannabis storefront at 560 Valencia St. for nearly a decade, is now on track to open one of San Francisco's first cannabis cafés — possibly the first of the new Amsterdam-style type in the Bay Area. Mission Local reported that Dolan anticipates beginning construction by September, pending final city permits. His proposed venue would feature cannabis-adjacent cuisine designed to complement the consumption experience, alongside live entertainment.

The legislation's passage marks the culmination of a lengthy permitting journey for Dolan, who first applied for a cannabis business permit with San Francisco's Office of Cannabis in 2018. The site at 560 Valencia has changed hands and tenants multiple times in the intervening years. Dolan's operational plan includes hiring individuals with past marijuana convictions as part of a restorative economic justice initiative.

The new café model is already operating in San Diego, West Hollywood, and Sacramento following passage of the state bill. If permitting and construction proceed on schedule, Dolan's Mission location could welcome its first customers as early as summer 2027. Neighbors and local business representatives have expressed mixed views, with some welcoming the economic activity in a long-vacant storefront and others raising concerns about indoor smoking and security.

topStories.headline: Portal Cinema Launches $250,000 Kickstarter, Eyes Late-October Opening in Bernal Heights
topStories.dek: The nonprofit arthouse theater coming to 3293 Mission St. has launched a crowdfunding campaign and is targeting a late October or November debut with 11 or more screenings per week.
topStories.body:
The Portal Cinema, a 49-seat nonprofit arthouse theater planned for 3293 Mission St. in Bernal Heights, has launched a Kickstarter campaign with a goal of raising $250,000 to fund an electrical panel upgrade, 35mm film projection, and a 5.1 surround-sound system — upgrades needed to open at full capacity this fall.

Founder and programmer Nellie Killian, an SF native who spent two decades in New York working for the Criterion Channel, the British Film Institute, and Metrograph, told the San Francisco Chronicle she hopes to open in late October or November. No firm date has been announced. Killian has been converting the 1,500-square-foot space — formerly a real estate office — since leasing it in 2023, navigating a lengthy city permitting process throughout.

The Portal's planned programming would blend new indie releases, global contemporary cinema, and repertory classics, presented in digital, 35mm, and 16mm formats, with 11 or more screenings per week. The cinema would join what has become a lively entertainment stretch of Mission Street, which also includes the Royal Cuckoo Organ Bar, El Rio, Emmy's Spaghetti Shack, and the performance space Magic Patio.

Beyond the Kickstarter, The Portal Cinema is also pursuing foundation grants, corporate sponsorships, and other philanthropic support. Those interested in supporting at an organizational level can reach Killian through theportalcinema.com.

topStories.headline: Bernal Heights Outdoor Cinema Returns for 22nd Season with Film Crawls and Free Screenings
topStories.dek: The volunteer-run festival kicks off with Film Crawls on Mission and Cortland in early September, followed by free neighborhood outdoor screenings through September 24.
topStories.body:
Bernal Heights Outdoor Cinema, the volunteer-driven festival showcasing local independent filmmakers since 2004, returns for its 22nd season with events running September 4 through September 24, 2026.

The season opens with a Film Crawl along Mission Street on September 4 and a second Film Crawl along Cortland Avenue on September 5, with an Under the Stars event on September 6 and the main outdoor screening season beginning September 10 through September 24. Venues — historically including Precita Park, Holly Park, Bernal Heights Park, Bernal Heights Playground, and community spaces along Mission and Cortland — will be confirmed closer to opening night.

All screenings are free and feature short films by local filmmakers selected by a volunteer committee from approximately 75 submissions reviewed over a five-week period, with filmmakers notified by early August. This year's season will include presentations of the Best of Bernal, Spirit of Bernal, and Bernal Bright Star awards, with audience voting at each screening.

The festival, which has brought together all corners of the socially and economically diverse neighborhood for more than two decades, is entirely volunteer-run. Those interested in helping with outreach, day-of support, or hospitality can contact the organization at info@bhoutdoorcine.org.

events.title: SF Community Music Center: Free Adult Open House

moreNews.headline: Smoke Shop Near 16th and Mission Stops Selling Tobacco After State Enforcement Visit
moreNews.body: A smoke shop operating without a required permit near 16th and Mission streets has stopped selling tobacco products following a visit by state enforcement officials, Mission Local reported in mid-August. The action is part of broader city and state efforts to address unlicensed retail around the 16th Street BART plaza corridor, where officials have been working to bring unpermitted commerce under control. The corridor has seen heightened enforcement this summer: SFPD has issued nearly 400 warnings and 56 citations to unpermitted street vendors since a new state law took effect in June, with city officials and nearby businesses reporting cleaner sidewalks and fewer sellers of suspected stolen merchandise.

moreNews.headline: Dance Mission Theater Opens Fall Season This Weekend with 'Talk Story'
moreNews.body: Dance Mission Theater, the women-led nonprofit performance venue on 24th Street, opens its fall 2026 season this weekend with 'Talk Story,' featuring new work by Sharp & Fine and guest artists, running August 28–30. The run launches a packed fall calendar at the theater, which is celebrating 25 years as a community arts anchor. Upcoming productions include Kathy Mata Ballet's free 'Giselle' on September 13, Rogelio López & Dancers returning September 18–20, and Sindhoor Natya's 'Encounter' September 25–27.

moreNews.headline: Bernal Connect Seeks Volunteer Plant Stewards for Recreation Center Green Installation
moreNews.body: Bernal Connect, the neighborhood community hub, is looking for volunteer stewards to tend to new planters installed at the Bernal Heights Recreation Center as part of a community-driven vision for a neighborhood town square. The campaign, announced in mid-August, invites residents to commit to regular watering and care of the green installation — described as a vital step toward a broader placemaking effort on the hill. Interested neighbors can learn more and sign up at bernalconnect.com.

restaurants.name: Royal Cuckoo Organ Bar

restaurants.name: El Farolito (Outer Mission)

shops.name: Dandelion Chocolate
shops.description: A craft chocolate maker on Valencia Street that sources cacao directly from farms and makes each bar in small batches on-site, with a factory store open to visitors.

shops.type: Mural arts center and gift shop

artEntertainment.description: A forthcoming 49-seat nonprofit arthouse cinema at 3293 Mission St. in Bernal Heights, targeting a late-October or November 2026 opening with indie, global, and repertory programming in digital, 35mm, and 16mm formats.

artEntertainment.name: Foreign Cinema (Courtyard Screenings)
